Hi Anna / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, attached is a first-pass capacity matrix that maps your stated SLAs and monthly token volumes to recommended deployment modes (Private VPC vs Dedicated reserved pools) and GPU footprint. The sheet has three scenarios: Pilot (low concurrency), Production baseline, and Peak (holiday month).

Key ask: could you confirm the expected 95th percentile concurrent requests and any hard constraints on outbound data plane egress (e.g., must remain within EU-only egress)? That drives whether we recommend Private (customer-managed VPC + on-prem option) or Dedicated (Redwood-reserved with region isolation).

Attachments: greenline_capacity_matrix.xlsx; redwood_private_vs_dedicated_onepager.pdf

Short summary recommendation (based on your notes):
- If your compliance team requires customer-hosted key material (HSM/KMS) + no external egress, go Private.
- If you want predictable throughput with SLA-backed latency and are OK with Redwood-managed infra inside EU, Dedicated is lower operational lead time and cost for the first 12 months.

I'll loop Dev for the GPU sizing specifics and Marissa for contract/term impacts.

Next steps: Anna, can you send the procurement PI and your preferred contract term (12 vs 36 months)? We'll produce a side-by-side cost estimate and a recommended rollout (canary -> full).

Thanks,
Hannah

Thanks Hannah. Quick dive on the GPU sizing assumptions I used in the matrix so the procurement team has transparency:

Assumptions (Production baseline):
- Avg prompt length: 75 tokens; avg completion: 60 tokens
- Target p95 latency: <= 500ms for chat-style requests
- Concurrent inference sessions (baseline): 120 active sessions; peak concurrency: 480
- Model family: LlamaX-13B quantized (int8) or equivalent — we provided model profiles in the sheet.

Sizing notes:
- Dedicated: 8x A100-80GB equiv nodes (multi-GPU pods, model sharding), gives ~3500 tok/s sustained and headroom for burst with autoscaling. Good fit if you need SLA and Redwood-managed K8s.
- Private: If you insist on customer KMS/HSM and no managed egress, customers typically provision 6x H100-80GB (on-prem or private cloud) to match similar throughput because the private stack has slightly higher overhead for KV cache management. We included a conservative 15% overhead.

Fallbacks / graceful degradation: we recommend a smaller fallback model (7B int4) if capacity constrained; that keeps latency SLAs while lowering cost.

Open technical questions for Greenline:
- Do you need full token-level audit logs retained for 7 years (GDPR/e-discovery)? That will affect storage and export bandwidth.
- Any hard limits on outbound telemetry to Redwood console? If telemetry is blocked, we need a holdback plan for observability.

I attached a short compliance checklist (audit_requirements_cd.pdf) referenced by Markus on the call.

- Dev

Thanks Hannah, Dev — useful level of detail. A few clarifications from procurement & infra: 

1) Greenline is EU-headquartered and requires EU-only processing and storage for cardholder-adjacent data. That pushes us to Private unless you can certify no egress and customer-managed KMS.

2) On concurrency: our BAU expectation is 80 concurrent sessions, but during batch settlements we can see short spikes to ~420 for ~10 minutes. We'll need autoscaling for that pattern.

3) Audit logs: legal requires 5 years for token-level audit but with redaction of PII. Is Redwood able to support server-side redaction before logs are exported?

4) Procurement: initial PO will target a 12-month term, but procurement asked for a cost delta between 12/24/36 mo. Please include CAPEX-style estimate for Private (one-time infra uplift) vs OPEX (Dedicated).

Would also like to loop in our cloud partner (Lars) to confirm private-cloud sizing assumptions. Lars, can you confirm whether Greenline's current IaaS contracts can support H100-80GB instances in EU region?

Best,

Anna — short note on the compliance checklist:

- KMS: If Greenline requires customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key), Private is the path. We can integrate with your Azure Key Vault HSM or on-prem HSM; we'll need discovery of key lifecycle policies.
- Audit logs: Redwood can perform server-side PII redaction using deterministic hashing prior to long-term retention. We'll need sample payloads to verify hashing doesn't break downstream analytics.
- Evidence package: For Private we provide installer logs + SCA of critical binaries. For Dedicated we provide SOC2 Type II report plus per-tenant audit export.

I'll attach a compact checklist in the SOW; Marissa / Hannah — please call out which items must be mandated in the contract vs which are implementation tasks.

Regards,
